agent.summary: Implemented PF_IO_CONTROL in xs-rs: exact --bwlimit/--timeout parsing, the token-bucket rate limiter, F_IO_CONFIG negotiation in the C++ order, negotiated keep-alives, and idle-timeout exit code 30. C++ clients and servers interoperate in both directions, and hostile or older peers are refused for invalid or unnegotiated keep-alives and malformed I/O configuration.
agent.diagnosis: The C++ reference in src/rate_limit.cpp, Conn::configure/check_timeout/writer, run_client and run_server, plus tests/io_limit_test.py defined the work. The previous xs-rs advertised no IO_CONTROL, sent no IO_CONFIG, accepted keep-alives unconditionally and had no rate or idle deadline; its receiver also wrote synchronously, so it could not emit heartbeats during long work. I matched the C++ frame order and rejection messages, added a writer thread for receiver-side heartbeats, and verified pacing with a measured 512 KiB transfer at 256 KiB/s that stayed above the 1.5 s floor.
agent.change: Added xs-wire/src/io_control.rs with parse_rate/parse_timeout, the RateLimiter token bucket, IoControl deadlines and heartbeat state, an ActivityReader, and a watchdog. Added --bwlimit and --timeout to xs-rs CLI/Options, negotiated IO_CONTROL, sent and validated IO_CONFIG first after HELLO, wired rate limiting and keep-alives into the writer, moved receiver output onto the same queued writer, and enforced idle exit 30. Extended integration coverage under rs/*/tests/.
agent.expected_effect: C++ xs with --bwlimit/--timeout can push to and pull from xs-rs; xs-rs can do the same against C++ xs. Wire writes are paced after compression, idle connections emit empty F_KEEPALIVE frames at one third of the deadline, blocked writers and idle readers expire with code 30, and invalid keep-alives or malformed IO_CONFIG are refused as protocol errors before a destination is created.
agent.risks: Timeout expiry is enforced by a watchdog that exits the process with code 30, matching the C++ exit status but without C++'s explicit peer SIGTERM or receiver temp-file cleanup on timeout. The rate bucket charges complete frames rather than C++'s occasional coalesced small-frame batch, which preserves the configured bytes-per-second over time but can differ by one bucket window.
agent.tests: Added 5 xs-wire io_control unit tests, 4 xs-wire/C++ integration tests (accepted IO config plus keep-alives; refusal of pre-config, non-empty and unnegotiated keep-alives; oversized/malformed IO config), and 5 xs-rs integration tests (four-way C++/Rust push and pull with IO control, measured rate pacing, client timeout exit 30, and Rust server keep-alive/config refusal).
